components.factual_paraphrase: Experiment 3: 22 dyslexic children were scanned before and after two eight-week periods. Order was randomized: reading then math n=8, math then reading n=6, reading then no intervention n=8. Math/no-intervention periods were pooled as control. Reading treatment was Seeing Stars, three hours/day, five days/week, emphasizing orthographic imagery and phonological awareness; the comparison was reading treatment versus control-period change, not magnocellular training.

components.factual_paraphrase: Reading-period gains included real-word reading, pseudoword reading and phonological awareness; no corresponding control-period gains. works.title: Accuracy of metacognitive monitoring affects learning of texts.

source.kind: journal PDF hosted by St Olaf teaching center

access.identity_verification: Physical first page visually verified: exact title, Keith W. Thiede/Mary C. M. Anderson/David Therriault, 2003, DOI 10.1037/0022-0663.95.1.66; Journal of Educational Psychology 95(1):66–73. All 8 physical pages visually read; numbered journal pages 66–73 include references and appendix, no first-page preview.

components.factual_paraphrase: Single experiment: 66 University of Illinois at Chicago students randomized by order of appearance to delayed-keyword, immediate-keyword, or no-keyword groups, $20 participation payment. Seven expository texts: one practice plus six critical texts. Keyword groups generated five gist keywords; delayed group read all six first, immediate group generated after each text. All groups received identical initial instructions, ease-of-learning judgments and pen/paper.

components.factual_paraphrase: Monitoring accuracy was the within-person Goodman-Kruskal gamma between comprehension ratings and initial test performance across texts. Delayed generation had higher accuracy than the immediate/no-keyword groups; overall F(2,63)=4.07, MSE=.26. Thus relative monitoring accuracy was an empirical component before the restudy and second-test components.

components.factual_paraphrase: After the initial test, participants received only aggregate number correct, selected which texts to reread, reread selected texts, then took a second test. The first test contained six questions/text (three details, three inference); the second contained twelve (six detail, six inference), including prior and new items. Regulation was separately indexed by gamma of judgment versus restudy selection: means -.79 delayed, -.35 immediate, -.36 no-keyword; F(2,58)=3.31, MSE=.41. Number of texts restudied did not differ reliably.
